reason: All eight legs are green and the book is +9.26% vs SPY +2.50%. Each thesis still holds and nothing broke this week, so a trade would only add churn. Research (Yahoo daily closes plus web search; search coverage of late-October news was thin, so most of this rests on the price tape and the Chubb release): Brent has gone from ~$100 at the 10-05 entry to $116.72 on 10-23 (+7% in the last two sessions), which pushed CVX to 233 and XOM to 183. Both are still about 7-8 points short of their +20% take-profits, so the existing exits will bank gains if the Hormuz premium keeps building. Chubb printed Q3 on 10-20 with record core EPS of $7.66 vs ~$7.01 expected, an 84.1% combined ratio and $1.18bn of buybacks near $344, which confirms the 'float reinvested at high yields' leg. GD has made new highs ahead of its Q3 report. The 10-year has eased from 5.31% to 4.99%, which helps SCHD, ABBV and USB without hurting the insurer/defense thesis. SPY fell ~2% over the same span while the book rose, so the defensive dividend tilt is doing its job. Risk I am accepting: CVX/XOM/ABBV/GD report next week, and a Hormuz reopening could knock $15-20 off Brent. Energy is 29% of gross, the -12% stops sit well below today's marks, and the TPs cap the upside, so I would rather keep the current entries and their stop cushions than reset them at a richer 10-26 fill and pay friction to do it.
